guide.summary: Internal use, one Zendesk account (self-serve, wait none); Public app for many Zendesk customers (app review, wait 1-3 weeks for new app submissions).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Internal use, one Zendesk account (self-serve, wait none). Hardest: Public app for many Zendesk customers (app review, wait 1-3 weeks for new app submissions).

composio.note: Composio lists Zendesk as having managed OAuth, which suits prototypes. For launch, use your own client ID and secret in a custom auth config.

need_own_app.answer: Not for prototypes, since Composio provides a managed Zendesk app. For production you should bring your own: a managed app shows Composio's name on consent and shares quota. Multi-customer distribution needs your own global client.
reasons: Consent screen shows Composio's name with a managed app
Managed app quota is shared across all Composio users
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval
Default scopes may not cover what you need
Distributing to multiple Zendesk customers requires your own global OAuth client

prerequisites.title: Zendesk admin account
prerequisites.detail: Creating an OAuth client requires admin access. A 14-day free trial is offered if you have no account.

prerequisites.title: Marketplace developer portal registration
prerequisites.detail: Register your organization at apps.zendesk.com and sign in before submitting an app. Sign-up works with email, Google or GitHub.

prerequisites.title: Sponsored developer account with d3v- prefix
prerequisites.detail: Requests from accounts without the d3v- prefix are not accepted. The local client identifier must start with zdg-.

prerequisites.title: Organization profile details
prerequisites.detail: Prepare partner types, short and long descriptions, regions, certification count and a company contact. Also have a privacy policy URL if you have one.

steps.title: Create local OAuth client in Admin Center
steps.detail: Sign in as a Zendesk admin and create the client. Set kind to Confidential, add your redirect URL, and save the identifier and secret.
steps.done_when: You have a client identifier and secret saved securely.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config through Composio's API using your client ID and secret. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard and check it matches the client exactly.
steps.done_when: The auth config exists and a test connection completes.

steps.title: Choose minimal scopes
steps.detail: List the Zendesk endpoints your agent calls and whether each needs read or write. Request only those scopes.
steps.done_when: A scope list is ready that matches the endpoints.

steps.title: Register on the Marketplace portal
steps.detail: Sign up at apps.zendesk.com and complete the organization profile.
steps.done_when: Your organization is registered and you are signed in.

steps.title: Submit global OAuth client request
steps.detail: In the portal choose Global OAuth, then Request new OAuth. Fill in every field on the local client, even ones labeled optional, and note the secret first.
steps.done_when: You receive an email and a ticket reference.

steps.title: Wait for Zendesk to convert the client
steps.detail: If approved, Zendesk converts your local client to global. No timeline is documented for this step.
steps.done_when: Zendesk confirms the client is global.

steps.title: Prepare app ZIP and submission answers
steps.detail: Package the source code in a ZIP and check branding guideline compliance. Draft the descriptions and compliance answers for you to review.
steps.done_when: The ZIP passes the automatic check with no red errors.

steps.title: Submit app and answer compliance questions
steps.detail: Upload the ZIP, answer all mandatory compliance questions accurately, and submit.

steps.title: Wait for Marketplace review
steps.detail: Zendesk says new submissions take 1-3 weeks. If approved, the listing goes live by 10am PST the next day.
steps.done_when: You receive approval or a rejection.

traps.title: Regular tokens are not allowed for multi-customer apps
traps.detail: Public and integration apps for multiple customers must use global OAuth tokens. Customers may not share their API credentials with you.

traps.title: You lose access to the client page after conversion
traps.detail: Once converted, only Zendesk's Marketplace Operations Team can edit the client. Note the secret and identifier before you submit.

traps.title: Scopes outside the allowed list fail
traps.detail: A scope outside the client's allowed scopes returns a 400 invalid_scope error and no token. Changing scopes after approval means contacting Zendesk Support.

traps.title: Possibly one global client only
traps.detail: A developer reported that only one global client could be requested, so prod, dev and staging may not all get one. Staff reportedly advised local clients for dev and staging.

traps.title: Use the exact production client identifier
traps.detail: The identifier should be the exact production value and represent your product. Names like zdg-global_client1 are not acceptable.

traps.title: Redirect URI must match exactly
traps.detail: The redirect URI in the request must exactly match the one on the client. Zendesk authorization is per customer subdomain, so you must know each customer's subdomain.

traps.title: Global client scope is limited to Support and Chat
traps.detail: The global client instructions apply only to Zendesk Support and Chat with Agent Workspace. Zendesk Sell needs a Multi-User Application, and Sunshine Conversations bots need a separate token.

traps.title: Composio callback cannot be verified by you
traps.detail: Zendesk requires exact redirect URI matching. If you want to hide Composio's domain, proxy the callback through your own domain with a 302 redirect to Composio.

blockers.symptom: Validation fails on submission with a generic 'something went wrong' error
blockers.what_it_means: The app ZIP check failed, and the portal gave no detail.
blockers.what_to_do: Open a Zendesk support ticket. Fix any red errors, then use Submit Update to resubmit.
blockers.agent_can_help: Check the ZIP contents against the branding and manifest requirements before uploading.

blockers.symptom: Global OAuth request page is hard to find or the link is broken
blockers.what_it_means: Zendesk's global client request documentation was reported as outdated.
blockers.what_to_do: In the Marketplace portal, choose Global OAuth then Request new OAuth. Contact Zendesk Support if it is missing.

blockers.symptom: Authorization fails with 400 Bad Request and invalid_scope
blockers.what_it_means: You asked for a scope outside the client's allowed scopes.
blockers.what_to_do: Request only allowed scopes, or edit the local client's allowed scopes in Admin Center. For a global client, contact Zendesk Support.
blockers.agent_can_help: Compare requested scopes against the client's allowed scopes.

open_questions: How long does Zendesk take to approve a global OAuth client request? No timeline was found; ask Zendesk Support or the Marketplace portal ticket.
Does a customer's admin need to approve or enable a global-client app? Docs only say the account owner authorizes for their subdomain; confirm with a test install.
Can several global clients (prod, dev, staging) be requested? Only a community anecdote exists; ask Zendesk Support.
Is a Marketplace listing strictly required for a private multi-customer integration, or does the global client alone suffice? Not clear from docs; ask Zendesk Marketplace support.
